Samir —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attaching a short matrix and a draft autoscale policy we can iterate on (see attached: edgeforge_trench_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx and proposed-autoscale-policy-redwood.pdf). High level answers here so your procurement and infra folks have something to review immediately: 

- Trench allocation: we carve ephemeral "trench" slabs from a global shoulder pool. During simultaneous spikes, we allocate proportionally to recent usage and committed throughput weight (your reserved slabs get priority, then short-window credits, then open shoulder).
- Eviction order: low-priority preemptible work (batch retrains) -> opportunistic ephemeral agents -> soft-eviction of shoulder slabs (30m notice) -> forced eviction only when capacity pressure is sustained > 12m.
- Fallback: we route to smaller quantized model variant automatically when latency SLO would otherwise be violated. This is included in the policy and preserves output semantics for ~85% of requests.
- Billing interplay: shoulder credits are consumed before overage billing; we provide a daily credit ledger export and monthly reconciliation line-item for any consumed shoulder above commit (sample amendment included).

Next steps: I'll sync Rishi and Karthik to get a short operations appendix with exact prewarm counts and the tail-latency run schedule. Can you confirm the forecast rows in the attached excel reflect your worst weekly peak and the nightly retrain windows?

Samir — quick ops note from Rishi (runtime):

We ran a similar carve for Helix last quarter; a couple specifics you can expect in the appendix:

- Prewarm counts: for your baseline commit (8 slabs reserved) we recommend 2 prewarm slabs per region during the 00:00–06:00 retrain window and 1 prewarm per region for daytime; this reduces cold-starts and keeps latency tails < P95=220ms in our tests.
- Eviction grace: we implement a soft 30-minute drain window for batch jobs and send a webhook 5 minutes prior to eviction to allow job checkpointing.
- Auto-quant fallback: model variants are pinned to a compatibility matrix; we will route to the quantized variant when projected tail latency exceeds configured SLO (default: P99 < 1.2s).

I've attached the ops appendix draft (short bullets) into the shared drive; Marissa — happy to coauthor the appendix with you for procurement.

—Rishi

Samir —

We've updated the ops appendix with two worked examples and a line-item invoice template (see attached spreadsheet). Short summary of the additions: 

- Proportional allocation nuance: long-term committed growth is represented as a "commit weight" (a signed multiplier) used alongside recent usage; by default weight=1.0 for commit-only customers, we set weight=1.25 for customers with documented commit ramp (your account will have weight=1.15 based on your Q3 plan). That guarantees a soft headroom bias without hard-reserving extra slabs.
- Invoicing example: 120% consumption over 72h => shoulder credits consumed = (0.2 * committed_units * hours); we show the daily credit ledger entry and the month-end line item with an example calculation, plus the optional capped-escrow approach if you want to prebuy shoulder credits to smooth billing.
- Tail-latency SLO: ops propose P99 < 1.2s when using shoulder; we also offer an add-on Fast-Path with dedicated prewarm for a 95th percentile P95 < 320ms (priced separately).

Next steps: Marissa will share the revised appendix and a one-page procurement amendment (legal-friendly) that shows sample language for shoulder consumption, cap, and escrow options. If that looks good, we can schedule a calibration call with your procurement and infra teams on Tuesday (Apr 16).

Regards,
